name: San Pedro Tidaá Mixtec
confidence_why: Nothing describes Tidaá stress itself: the only work with Tidaá data is Josserand's 1983 comparative survey, whose family-wide statement that the Mixtec couplet carries stress on its first syllable is known only as quoted by Carroll 2015 and Penner 2019, so any placement for Tidaá is an inference from the family, not a finding.
catalog_citation: Josserand, Judy Kathryn. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History (Proto-Mixtec and Modern Mixtec Text). PhD diss., Tulane University, p. 180 -- quoted second-hand in Carroll, Lucien Serapio. 2015. Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec Word Prosody. PhD diss., UC San Diego (eScholarship 0bs6b7mt), section 4.2.1, p. 86; Tidaá as a Josserand survey town: Carroll 2015, Table A.2, p. 276.
catalog_locator: Carroll 2015: p. 86, section 4.2.1 'Default stress' (under 4.2 'Survey of stress descriptions in Mixtec varieties'); couplet definition p. 85; Yoloxochitl exception p. 87; Table A.2 p. 276 Josserand 1983 p. 180 itself NOT seen (ProQuest/UMI only).
catalog_quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. Besides the data from Santo Domingo Nuxaa shown in (4.2), several other descriptions support the characterization of stress in Mixtec as falling on the first vowel of the couplet. ... In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. [Table A.2, p. 276, row] San Pedro Tidaá Tid Tida mtx Alta:E

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable (first mora) of the bimoraic root 'couplet', i.e. root-initial / penultimate-of-couplet stress, as generalized for all Mixtec varieties surveyed; no Tidaá-specific evidence exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Tidaá. Carroll (p. 86) notes that in some varieties (Ayutla, Mixtepec) first-syllable prominence is realized as lengthening/devoicing and can be tone-dependent; nothing said for Tidaá.
new_statements.domain_note: Family-wide generalization over Josserand's 130-variety survey (which includes San Pedro Tidaá, Carroll Table A.2 p. 276), not a description of Tidaá; the 'couplet' is the bimoraic/disyllabic root (word-level citation forms). Tidaá itself has never been described: Glottolog 0 descriptive refs, LingMex 0, OLAC no deposit, SIL no materials; MixteCoDB's only Tidaá source is the Josserand wordlist.
new_statements.identity_note: The only statement whose scope covers Tidaá is Josserand's (1983:180) family-wide couplet definition, reported second-hand by Carroll 2015:86; it is not a description of Tidaá. Tidaá [mtx, tida1235] = San Pedro Tidaá / Santiago Tidaá, Nochixtlán district; Auderset et al. 2023 group it in 'Linkage 5' with Diuxi-Tilantongo [xtd, diux1235], the nearest variety with a first-hand stress description (Pike & Oram 1976). Ethnologue: 'Dialects: None known'.
